chapter: Buck and Bubbles: Nazarro and Bubbles
title: Bubbles' cramp rolls and heel drops
summary: Green describes Bubbles' heel-dropping cramps, the kick cramp and the half-tempo time step called rhythm tap.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: But I'm curious to know, what was Bubbles doing with rhythms that was different from other dancers had done before, and what was it you just demonstrated that shows that?

Well, it was -- he involved the heel, the dropping of the heels, you see, into what he called cramps, cramping, like that. And like what they call a break. Like after you do a step, you would do a break, and that's where he involved this cramping.
Then he had the kick cramp, where you kick the foot
out. And that's that last part of it there where we -- you kick the foot out, and you get a cramp, see. And then you turn and you get another kind of cramp. That's the dropping of the heels, see.

And the time step, instead of it being up tempo, it was half of the tempo, you see. He called it that, rhythm tap dance, see, at that time, you see. And -- well, he was teaching me. I was asking him to teach me how to do -- it was his idea. He says, 'What's the matter with your partner? Why don't he like to dance?'
